subject.name_or_desc: A gentlewoman whose husband was at sea; she was herself extremely disfigured by smallpox, weak-eyed, full of grief for her husband, and chronically ill (Saturn, lord of her 6th, retrograde — she relapsed from one disease into another)

context.question: A woman asked of her husband at sea: if alive, where, and when shall he return?
context.asked_at: Not stated in the text (the death Lilly timed from the figure fell on 8 October following)
context.setting: She asked Lilly about her absent husband; Lilly judged both the husband's state and, from the same figure, her own fate

attachments.key_positions: The 7th house taken as the woman's ascendant in this question; Saturn lord of the 6th retrograde; the husband's significator (the Sun, per Lilly's prose) in her hayz and free from all affliction; Mars and Saturn moving to an ill aspect, Mars then near the place of the Moon in the question (about 2° of a sign) and Saturn in about 2° of Capricorn, the Moon at that (later) moment in about 20°
attachments.note: Positions partly garbled in the 1647 OCR; the husband's significator being wholly unafflicted and the timing of the wife's death are the two points Lilly states unambiguously.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
